Codex review: blocked before merge. ## What this changes This PR removes duplicate config and database lifecycle bookkeeping while reusing existing writers and history readers. **Example:** Capture a read of /tmp/openclaw-a/openclaw.json, then change OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH to /tmp/openclaw-b/openclaw.json. - **Before:** The captured read rejects because its environment selector changed. - **After:** The captured read completes using openclaw-a; a subsequent reload selects openclaw-b. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Approved direction and substantial owner-level coverage, with a confirmed test migration defect and incomplete upgrade qualification. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Maintainer authorship exempts ordinary media proof; config loading and recovery changes still need fresh-install and stable-upgrade evidence preserving settings, backups, and pending user turns. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Refactor · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Repeated admission and lifecycle machinery adds runtime work and maintenance complexity around otherwise unchanged config and session operations. **Reason:** The feature-history owner approves the direction and documents the accepted tradeoffs; the diff consolidates existing responsibilities without adding settings or public APIs. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 3 items remain** Keep open: this maintainer-approved simplification remains useful, but an unmigrated ACP test expectation causes a confirmed CI failure. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `f3bf14b01d1a8512a583c058f2858cf2f92fd127` ## Before merge - [ ] **Align the ACP selector test with captured-read semantics (P2)** - Removing selector fencing makes the ACP config case resolve with its captured configuration after OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH changes during the metadata join. The unchanged test still requires rejection at src/acp/runtime/session-meta-read.test.ts:260, and exact-head CI confirms this failure. Split that case into a positive captured-source assertion while preserving the caller- and store-revocation cases. - [ ] **Complete next step** - Determine whether the Advisor guidance UI timeout is caused by this diff using matching base evidence, and repair it only if causation is established. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade. Show that existing data still loads and works with this change. ## Findings - [P2] Align the ACP selector test with captured-read semantics — `src/config/io.runtime.ts:137` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: No fresh-install and v2026.10.4 upgrade run demonstrates config recovery and pending-input continuity with existing settings and data intact.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Gateway and CLI callers load captured configuration and session facts through shared-state writers and retained history workers, receiving configuration, health metadata, and transcript results. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Gateway and CLI callers] --> B[Captured config reader] B --> C[Health and audit writer] C --> D[Shared state database] A --> E[Retained history reader] E --> F[Agent session database] B --> G[Caller results] E --> G ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain the approved simplification and align the remaining ACP selector test with captured-read semantics. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Exact-head CI and the ACP fixture establish the selector-expectation mismatch; no local execution or current-main product failure is claimed. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The existing-owner approach matches repository policy and recorded maintainer direction; updating the stale ACP expectation avoids restoring intentionally removed fencing. Full review comments: - [P2] Align the ACP selector test with captured-read semantics — `src/config/io.runtime.ts:137` Removing selector fencing makes the ACP config case resolve with its captured configuration after OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH changes during the metadata join. The unchanged test still requires rejection at src/acp/runtime/session-meta-read.test.ts:260, and exact-head CI confirms this failure. Split that case into a positive captured-source assertion while preserving the caller- and store-revocation cases. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.94 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [663b7766cf49](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/663b7766cf4904da8bac733d938bd5e546966289). ### Provenance checked - `Config observation and recovery` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (dbde270238dbbf5baa3672c8e46f0c958144383c: Offload health and audit persistence while preventing superseded observations from committing stale metadata.) - `Captured config selector fencing` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (6718352a63df815940c7a7bc5666f6484c7b8d9a: Prepare configuration asynchronously while retaining source and publication checks; this PR explicitly adopts captured-source semantics for ambient selector changes.) - `Warm schema admission` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (c828f7ed1d560295f78166a98fb54687dc162b28: Carry admitted schema facts across cached accesses while detecting schema changes; the new policy assigns validation to physical admission and explicit repair.) - `Shared-worker relocation` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (b140acb1ea3b7c4f39ca48930fb17ac3338dcd2a: Prevent workers reopening retired paths and settle stale actors before replacement; this PR explicitly accepts close/reopen recovery for active relocation.) - `Pending-input custody reconciliation` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (84af47269371dbc3cd8662b1f7203200a474c64d: Move reconciliation into the writer and protect live custody through host grants; the replacement relies on the existing physical FIFO and current owner selection.) - `Transcript executor borrowing` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (d94fe35027e7f04c3220bfb7794097e01460b4e5: Retain physical transcript identity and generation through asynchronous reads; this PR keeps history ownership and matching lock ordering while removing unrelated executor lifetime coupling.) - `Cold-storage inventory` keeps the original intent (c3f2837f569ed3a485ad5550a1fb1e9c13210b09: Read durable inventory through workers while preserving source ownership; consolidation retains those responsibilities.) - `Private MCP mutation forwarding` keeps the original intent (3ca3b97a21d4f9216b199b90a473ad43f085dd35: Share the MCP mutation pipeline; removing the forwarding helper preserves the same pipeline and outer lifecycle facade.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence Acceptance criteria: - pnpm test src/acp/runtime/session-meta-read.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 - pnpm test src/config/io.runtime-async.test.ts src/config/io.runtime-models.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 - git diff --check What I checked: - **Pinned introduction and current-main comparison:** The introduced diff removes selector fencing, observation supersession, duplicate schema admission, worker rebinding, and unrelated executor borrowing; fetched main retains those mechanisms. ([`src/config/io.runtime.ts:137`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f3bf14b01d1a8512a583c058f2858cf2f92fd127/src/config/io.runtime.ts#L137), [f3bf14b01d1a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f3bf14b01d1a8512a583c058f2858cf2f92fd127)) - **Confirmed diff-caused CI failure:** The exact-head compact job reports that the ACP retired-config case resolves instead of rejecting; its fixture changes OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH while a metadata join is held, directly exercising the intentionally removed selector fence. ([`src/acp/runtime/session-meta-read.test.ts:260`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f3bf14b01d1a8512a583c058f2858cf2f92fd127/src/acp/runtime/session-meta-read.test.ts#L260), [f3bf14b01d1a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f3bf14b01d1a8512a583c058f2858cf2f92fd127)) - **Recorded acceptance of snapshot tradeoffs:** The maintainer-authored body accepts captured-selector semantics and reduced bookkeeping; the predecessor explicitly also accepts returning a completed watermark after internal owner closure, so that historical concern is not repeated as a defect. Discussion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174039. ([f3bf14b01d1a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f3bf14b01d1a8512a583c058f2858cf2f92fd127)) - **Remaining effect boundaries:** Recovery checks original config and backup bytes before replacement; health updates preserve original maintenance exceptions; pending-history reconciliation retains the physical writer FIFO, conditional updates, and committed receipts. ([`src/config/io.observe-recovery-effects.ts:27`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f3bf14b01d1a8512a583c058f2858cf2f92fd127/src/config/io.observe-recovery-effects.ts#L27), [f3bf14b01d1a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f3bf14b01d1a8512a583c058f2858cf2f92fd127)) - **CI attribution limits:** The UI job times out waiting for Advisor guidance notices; available main comparisons skipped that lane, so inheritance or PR causation is unproven. Job-log retrieval was blocked by its storage redirect, but GitHub annotations were readable. The PR-context failure requests body evidence and is process-only; PostgreSQL conformance now passes. ([f3bf14b01d1a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f3bf14b01d1a8512a583c058f2858cf2f92fd127)) - **Policy and ownership:** Root and applicable docs, Gateway, server-methods, and SDK instructions were read; no maintainer-notes directory exists. History identifies Peter Steinberger as the principal contributor across these mechanisms, including their earlier names. ([`AGENTS.md:1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/663b7766cf4904da8bac733d938bd5e546966289/AGENTS.md#L1), [663b7766cf49](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/663b7766cf4904da8bac733d938bd5e546966289)) ### PR surface Source -505, Tests -353, Docs -1. ### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus test LOC** | Production +475/-980; tests +382/-735 | Production shrinks by removing duplicate mechanisms; added tests cover source preservation, rollback, and recovered pending-input ownership. | ### Root-cause cluster Relationship: `canonical` Canonical: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175077 Summary: This PR is the explicitly designated successor to the withdrawn candidate. Members: - `superseded`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174039 - Closed unmerged; its updated disposition assigns current implementation and qualification to this successor. Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything. ### Labels Label changes: - add `P2`: Useful internal simplification with a focused CI repair; no urgent user-facing regression was established. - add `rating: 🦪 silver shellfish`: Overall readiness is 🦪 silver shellfish; proof is 🦐 gold shrimp and patch quality is 🦪 silver shellfish. - add `status: ⏳ waiting on author`: ClawSweeper has contributor-facing work open and is waiting for author action. Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality; ✨ marks media proof (a screenshot, video, or linked artifact) that directly shows the changed behavior. ### Workflow ClawSweeper edits this one comment on every review.
